profile.headline: Senior Systems Software Engineer at NVIDIA
profile.summary:
I’m a Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA in Santa Clara, California, specializing in cloud technologies, storage solutions, and DevOps. I hold a Bachelor of Applied Science (Honours) in Computer Engineering from the University of Waterloo and have built a diverse portfolio of software development experience across multiple domains in both Canada and the USA. When I am not working, you will find me at the nearest ice rink playing hockey.

http://maxwellcarter.com
https://github.com/maxcarter

positions.title: Senior Systems Software Engineer - NTS
positions.description:
• NVIDIA GPU Network (NGN) Tenant Services team
• Engineer and support production storage services critical to NVIDIA's GeForce Now cloud gaming platform, content delivery, automated patching, and high-performance game streaming at scale.
• Develop and maintain GPU accelerated virtual machine images (VMI). The VMIs are used for various GeForce Now cloud gaming and AI use cases. 
• Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering teams to build innovative software solutions and automation frameworks that accelerate GPU cloud computing initiatives across NVIDIA's ecosystem.

positions.title: Systems Software Engineer 2 - NGN IPSE
positions.description:
• NVIDIA GPU Network (NGN) Infrastructure Performance & Storage Engineering (IPSE) team
• Service owner of a storage web service in the NVIDIA GeForce Now (GFN) cloud gaming service. The service plays an important role in enabling game platform streaming.
• Build software solutions in Python, C#, Java, and various other programming languages.

positions.title: Systems Software Engineer - NGN IPSE
positions.description:
• NVIDIA GPU Network (NGN) Infrastructure Performance & Storage Engineering (IPSE) team
• Supported a multi-petabyte scale Ceph storage cluster. The cluster hosted deep learning datasets to enable cloud based GPU accelerated artificial intelligence.
• Built software solutions in Python, C#, and Java that enabled storage provisioning for various NGN cloud use cases.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern - NGN IPSE
positions.description:
• NVIDIA GPU Network (NGN) Infrastructure Performance & Storage Engineering (IPSE) team
• Built an automation system in Python for deploying Ceph virtual storage clusters in the NVIDIA GPU Network. The system provided a serviceable way to quickly create filesystem storage for hosting deep learning datasets for the NVIDIA GPU Cloud (NGC). 
• Worked with Kibana to visualize various key performance indicators for an NVIDIA GPU Network storage service. The dashboard provided improved metric visualization and introduced automated alerts for unexpected service behaviour.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern - NGN GIA
positions.description:
• NVIDIA GPU Network (NGN) GPU Infrastructure Automation (GIA) team
• Developed a web service in C# ASP.NET that provided storage on demand. The service played an important role in enabling gaming platform streaming on the NVIDIA GeForce Now cloud gaming system. 
•  Built Kerberos as a Service using Pythonic RESTful API development. The service enabled Kerberos authentication cryptography in NVIDIA GPU Network storage systems.
• Designed and developed a self-service web portal using Vue.js and Node.js. The portal improved the NVIDIA DGX-1 Saturn V user on-boarding experience.

positions.title: Software Developer Intern - Lesson Activity Builder
positions.description:
• Designed and developed Game Show, an engaging educational game for SMART Boards using jQuery. The game placed first in the company wide intern project competition and was released to production as part of the SMART Learning Suite.

• Redesigned the SMART Lesson Activity Builder iOS native application for a new sign-in process. The application improved the connection experience for students joining a classroom activity from their mobile devices.

positions.title: Software Development Student - Network Operations Centre
positions.description:
• Developed a consolidated messaging web application in AngularJS. The application reduced cycles and normalized communication in the BlackBerry Network Operations Centre. 

• Created a scalable Model-View-Controller architecture for a PHP RESTful API. The architecture simplified various DevOps tool integrations for services across the BlackBerry Network Operations Centre. 

• Developed an extension to an existing service alert visualization web application in AngularJS with ElasticSearch integrations. The extension allowed users to create, read, update, and delete actions that could be associated to service alerts and define resolutions.

positions.title: Systems Software Development Student - Service Assurance Solutions
positions.description:
• Created a data orchestration system in Python using automated StackStorm workflows with various DevOps micro-services integrations. The system centralized service alert data and improved incident visibility and response time. 

• Built an administration tool web application in AngularJS supported by a PHP RESTful API. The tool improved management of the BlackBerry Network Operations Centre’s service monitoring wall. 

• Integrated JavaScript task management and automation into web applications using GruntJS. The integration helped improve productivity by automating code validation, end-to-end testing, and automatic deployment.

positions.title: Front-End Developer Intern - Quality Assurance
positions.description: • Built a dashboard web application using the JavaScript MEAN development stack. The dashboard improved the testing visibility for many aspects of industry leading interior design software.

projects.title: SleepyZzz - Infant Sleep Monitor
projects.description:
This was our Fourth Year Design Project (FYDP) at the University of Waterloo. The objective of this project was to design a monitoring system for infants to wear while they sleep to track their vitals and notify parents should anything go wrong. The system tracked the infant’s heart rate, movement, and body temperature. If the baby’s heart rate suddenly drops, or they roll over on their stomach, or develop a fever, the system would notify the parents within a reasonable amount of time so that they can quickly react and mitigate the problem.

The project was split into three main subsystems: the Embedded System, the Backend Services, and the Mobile Application.

The Embedded System focused on a microprocessor measuring and filtering sensor input and wirelessly outputting the data, over a secure network to the infant’s guardian’s mobile devices. The sensors enclosed in the Embedded system measure the infant’s heart rate, movement, and body temperature.

The Backend Services acted as a bridge and serve the purpose of connecting the Embedded System and the Mobile Application by means of cloud services.

The Mobile Application provided a means for notifying the guardian of potential health irregularity of the sleeping infant. When not in use, the application ran as a background task on the mobile device and interfaces directly with notification services to ensure the guardian is notified immediately, should something go wrong.
